title: The Last General
tagline: Rome's final military genius fought enemies on every front — including his emperor.

scenes.text: Constantinople, 527 CE. Emperor Justinian I sits upon the throne of a crumbling empire. The Western Roman Empire has fallen. But Justinian has a dream — reconquest. And he has one general capable of making it real.

scenes.speaker: Emperor Justinian
scenes.text: Belisarius. You are my sword. Reconquer Africa. Reconquer Italy. Give me back the Empire of Augustus.

scenes.speaker: Belisarius
scenes.text: The Vandals think themselves safe behind the sea. Let them think so a little longer. I will take Carthage before they have time to prepare.

challenge.instruction: Belisarius: raise the wall without gaps.
challenge.fact: Belisarius retook North Africa (533 CE), Italy (536–540 CE), and part of Spain — temporarily reuniting the old Western Roman Empire under Constantinople. He did it with armies far smaller than his opponents'.

scenes.text: Belisarius defeated armies many times larger than his own through speed, tactics, and the trust he inspired in his soldiers. He conquered North Africa in two years — a campaign that shocked the world.

challenge.instruction: Command Belisarius's amber forces. Outmaneuver the enemy to victory.
challenge.fact: Belisarius won battles against overwhelming odds through disciplined positioning, feigned retreats, and flanking strikes — tactics centuries ahead of his time.

scenes.speaker: Belisarius
scenes.text: They have accused me of treason three times now. Three times I have served with perfect loyalty. An emperor who doubts his best general is an emperor who has already lost. But I serve. It is what I am.

challenge.fact: Byzantine siege engineers used torsion catapults and trebuchets that required precise angle and distance calculations. A few degrees off meant the difference between destroying a gate or overshooting the wall.

scenes.text: Belisarius's supply lines stretched across the Mediterranean. Master the routing of his forces through the Byzantine corridors to reach the final objective...

challenge.fact: HuaRong Road (华容道) is a Chinese sliding puzzle based on Cao Cao's escape after the Battle of Red Cliffs in 208 AD — one of the most analyzed puzzles in combinatorics.

challenge.instruction: Belisarius always faced superior numbers. Deploy your archers and catapults before the battle begins — then launch the attack and watch your strategy unfold.
challenge.fact: Belisarius reconquered North Africa, Italy, and Spain for Emperor Justinian with armies of 10,000–15,000 against forces of 100,000+. He relied on disciplined cavalry and coordinated missile fire — tactics that anticipated modern combined arms.

scenes.speaker: Belisarius
scenes.text: Batu Khan waits at Krakow, but nothing is happening there, and without an event there is no fight. I will go first; the turn after I arrive, play the Battlefield card on Krakow and we attack.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 3 · Starting an Event. Deploy Belisarius to Krakow and End Turn. Next turn play the Battlefield card there, add your follower and win one attack.
challenge.fact: Event cards start a scenario at a location where you already have a Great Person, and only one who arrived on an earlier turn can start it. A local event keeps running until a player ends it.
